raw.abstractText:
Background

Tibial transverse osteotomy (TTO) is a promising but limited surgical option for diabetic foot (DF). Berberine, a natural compound from Coptis chinensis, exhibits anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects relevant to metabolic diseases.

Objectives

This study aimed to evaluate whether adjunctive berberine enhances the therapeutic outcomes of TTO in DF patients and to explore its potential association with the platelet-derived growth factor-B (PDGF-B)/PDGF receptor-β (PDGFRβ) signaling pathway.

Methods

This was a prospective, single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, blinded trial. Of 200 screened DF patients, 96 eligible participants (Wagner grade 2-4) scheduled for TTO were randomized 1:1 to receive either TTO plus local berberine injections (n=48) or TTO plus local saline placebo (n=48). An additional non-randomized diabetic reference group (n=10) and healthy control group (n=10) were included for exploratory cellular studies only. The primary outcome was the total effective rate of ulcer healing at 3 months. Secondary outcomes included changes in Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI), ulcer area, Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score and serum inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, IL-6). Exploratory outcomes comprised serum VEGF, bFGF and PDGF-B levels, as well as fibroblast apoptosis in wound tissue.

Results

All 96 randomized participants completed the 3-month follow-up, with no dropouts. The berberine group demonstrated a significantly higher total effective rate than the surgery-alone group (87.5% vs. 68.8%; risk difference, 18.7%; 95% CI, 1.2% to 36.2%; P < 0.05). At 3 months, the berberine group also showed greater improvements in ABI (mean difference, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.08 to 0.18; P < 0.01) and ulcer healing rate (mean difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 9.5% to 23.9%; P < 0.01), along with more significant reductions in hs-CRP and IL-6. Berberine treatment was associated with reduced fibroblast apoptosis in wound tissue (mean difference, -1.10%; 95% CI, -1.56% to -0.64%; P = 0.001) and lower protein expression of PDGF-B and PDGFRβ. No severe adverse events related to berberine injections were reported.

Conclusion

In DF patients undergoing TTO, adjunctive local berberine therapy significantly improves the total effective rate and promotes ulcer healing, with benefits associated with reduced inflammation and fibroblast apoptosis and downregulation of the PDGF-B/PDGFRβ pathway. These findings are correlative and require further mechanistic validation. Larger multi-center trials are needed to confirm efficacy and safety.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Liver fibrosis is a chronic wound healing process of liver injury and gut-liver axis dysregulation has been recently identified as an important contributor to liver fibrosis progression. Quercetin has been reported to have anti-inflammatory activity and microbiota-modulating effects. However, the potential targets of quercetin remain unclear, as does the relationship between quercetin-associated targets and changes in the gut microbiota in liver fibrosis.

Objectives

The purpose of this study was to use network pharmacology to predict potential targets of quercetin associated with liver fibrosis and to explore changes in gut microbiota following treatment with quercetin using a CCl4-induced rat model.

Methods

Eighteen male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into CON group, MOD group and QR group (n = 6 per group). Liver fibrosis was induced by weekly subcutaneous injection of carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) for eight weeks. Oral gavage of quercetin (50 mg/kg/day) was performed in QR group. Histopathological changes were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin staining, Masson staining and Ishak scoring. Potential targets of quercetin were screened using network pharmacology, followed by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction and Gene Ontology (GO)/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Cecal microbiota composition was determined by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Parametric or non-parametric tests were used accordingly, including one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test.

Results

Histopathology revealed significant liver injury and fibrosis in the MOD group relative to the CON group. The QR group showed lower Ishak fibrosis scores and milder histopathological features compared with the MOD group. Network pharmacology analysis identified UBC, UBE2I, RBX1, PSMB7 and UBA1 as hub targets, with KEGG pathways of interest including the TNF signaling pathway, p53 signaling pathway, Toll-like receptor signaling pathway and ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis. Alpha diversity of the cecal microbiota differed significantly among groups, whereas beta diversity did not. Relative abundance of Proteobacteria decreased and Firmicutes increased in the QR group relative to the MOD group. Taxa enrichment analysis identified enrichment of Muribaculaceae and Ligilactobacillus in the QR group.

Conclusion

Histopathology and microbiome analyses indicated that quercetin intervention was associated with altered liver histopathological features and shifts in gut microbiota composition in rats with CCl4-induced liver fibrosis. Network pharmacology predicted several hub targets and pathways potentially linked to these observations. As the present analyses are purely correlational and lack mechanistic validation at the molecular level, no causal relationships are implied between the predicted targets/pathways and the observed histological or microbiome changes. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrant further validation studies.

Background

 Fibrotic liver is one of the serious pathophysiological consequences of chronic injury to the liver, may progress toward serious complications including cirrhosis and hepatic carcinoma.

Objectives

Panax notoginseng is used for both therapeutic and prophylactic purposes in TCM; it is a source of Dencichine, an active substance that has been proven to exhibit antifibrotic properties in hepatic fibrosis. The present study investigated how Dencichine treatment ameliorates liver fibrosis using an animal model and a cellular fibrosis model.

Methods

Randomly assigned, male C57BL/6J mice received 10% CCl4 for 15 consecutive weeks to induce hepatic fibrosis. Treatment with Dencichine was initiated from 7th week onward. To simulate in-vitro the presence of a fibrotic microenvironment, LX-2 cells were treated with PDGF-BB at a concentration of 20 ng/mL and incubated from one up to four days and then treated by various doses of Dencichine. Liver function was evaluated by measuring alanine aminotransferase (ALT), AST, HA and LN. Histopathology was evaluated by haematoxylin/eosin (HE), Masson's trichrome and Sirius red stains. Quantitative real-time PCR and western blot analyses were used to evaluate mRNA and protein expression levels, respectively. Wound-healing assays and transwell chamber experiments were used to assess cell migration; EdU proliferation detection and flow cytometry were performed to measure cell proliferation and cell cycle, respectively.

Results

 The most important results are a considerable reduction of serum concentrations of AST and ALT, HA and laminin in CCl4-treated mice decreased liver injury and ECM deposition. Furthermore, this compound downregulated the expression of cyclin D1 and cyclin E1 and blocked the activation of PI3K and AKT kinases in fibrotic liver cells.

Conclusion

These results indicate that Dencichine may slow the development of liver fibrosis by interfering with the PI3K-AKT signaling cascade, demonstrating significant anti-scarring properties.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Ulcerative colitis is a relapsing inflammatory bowel disease driven by dysregulated immunity, epithelial barrier injury and microbial imbalance. Current therapies remain limited by relapse, adverse effects and incomplete response. Quercetin has anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective activities and ERK-MMP signaling may link inflammation to mucosal tissue damage.

Objectives

To evaluate whether the protective effects of quercetin in experimental ulcerative colitis (UC) are associated with modulation of ERK-MMP signaling, while avoiding causal overinterpretation beyond the animal and cellular evidence.

Methods

A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse model and a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophage inflammatory model were used. Mice were allocated to the control, UC model and low-, medium- and high-dose quercetin groups. Disease activity index (DAI; unitless), colon length, histopathology, inflammatory cytokines and ERK/MMP-related molecules were evaluated by histological staining, ELISA, qRT-PCR and western blotting. In-vitro, quercetin was compared with the ERK phosphorylation inhibitor U0126 and an agonistic stimulus to explore pathway-related associations. The study was exploratory and did not include genetic rescue experiments or human validation.

Results

In DSS-treated mice, medium- and high-dose quercetin were associated with improved colon morphology, reduced DAI scores and partial restoration of colon length. Quercetin decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and increased IL-10 expression. In both mouse colon tissues and LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, quercetin was associated with reduced ERK1/2 activation and lower MMP-3 and MMP-9 expression, together with partial recovery of TIMP expression. These molecular changes were directionally consistent with the effects observed after ERK inhibition in-vitro.

Conclusion

Quercetin showed protective effects in experimental UC models and these effects may be associated with modulation of the ERK-MMP signaling axis. Further pathway-specific rescue experiments, pharmacokinetic studies and human-relevant models are required before this mechanism can be considered definitive or clinically translatable.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Sarcopenia and frailty are frequent in patients with liver cirrhosis and are associated with morbidity and mortality. Given the limitations of computed tomography (CT) for routine assessment of muscle loss and the need for practical bedside assessment, we aimed to compare sonographic muscle thickness measurement and the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) for their prognostic value in patients with liver cirrhosis.

Methods

In this study, data of prospectively recruited patients with liver cirrhosis (both in- and outpatients) treated at a tertiary care centre were retrospectively analysed. Sonographic muscle thickness measurement was used to calculate the feather thigh muscle thickness index (fTMTI) and the compression thigh muscle thickness index (cTMTI). Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale. Patients were followed for liver transplantation or death.

Results

In total, 153 patients were included with a median Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) of 18 (Interquartile range (IQR) 10; 24). Ninety-five patients (62.0%) were male, and 70 patients (46%) were recruited in the outpatient setting. During the 90-day follow-up period, 71 patients (46.4%) either died or underwent liver transplantation. Outpatients had more muscle mass than inpatients and a lower CFS (fTMTI 19.1 mm/m vs. 12.1 mm/m, p < 0.001 and CFS 3 vs. 5, p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox-regression models adjusted for age and MELD score, a higher CFS remained independently associated with mortality and liver transplantation (LT) (HR 1.25 (1.14; 1.63), p < 0.001), whereas fTMTI and cTMTI were not consistently associated with a poorer prognosis (fTMTI HR 1.52 (0.68; 3.42), p = 0.300; cTMTI HR 1.01 (0.61; 1.68), p > 0.9). Subgroup analyses in men confirmed a superior prognostic value of CFS (HR 1.51 (1.17; 1.94), p = 0.001) over sonographic muscle thickness measurement (cTMTI HR 0.94 (0.84; 1.04), p = 0.200; fTMTI HR 0.93 (0.88; 1.00), p = 0.039).

Conclusion

CFS is robustly associated with poorer prognosis in patients with liver cirrhosis and seems to be superior to sonographic muscle thickness measurement of the thigh.

raw.abstractText: Shugan Formula (SGF) shows clinical hepatoprotective effects, but its mechanism against anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ATB-DILI) remains unclear. This study employed LC-MS/MS-based metabolomics to investigate SGF's protective effects in rats. ATB-DILI was induced by oral isoniazid and rifampicin (100 mg·kg<sup>-1</sup> each) for 14 days. During modeling, the rats in the treated groups received low, medium, or high doses of SGF via oral gavage, whereas the PC group was administered obeticholic acid. Serum biomarkers (ALT, AST, IL-6, IL-10, and TNF-α), hepatic oxidative stress markers (MDA, SOD, GST, and GSH-Px), liver histopathology, and serum metabolomics were assessed. SGF treatment significantly reduced serum ALT, AST, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels, decreased hepatic MDA and GST levels, and increased SOD and GSH-Px activities. Metabolomics revealed that SGF attenuated metabolic perturbations induced by liver injury, with the high-dose group being most effective. Key pathways involved amino acid metabolism, bile acid metabolism, and glycerophospholipid metabolism. This study provides scientific evidence for SGF in preventing and treating ATB-DILI.

raw.abstractText: This study aimed to explore the processing mechanism of single medicinal herbs in compound prescriptions, compare the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic changes of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula before and after processing, and elucidate its underlying mechanism against gastric ulcers. The results showed that six components, namely, corydaline, coptisine chloride, palmatine, berberine chloride, phellopterin, and imperatorin, exerted anti-ulcer activities. The optimal vinegar-processing parameters for Corydalis yanhusuo were determined as follows: processing temperature of 84°C, vinegar dosage of 37%, and baking time of 35 min. Vinegar-processed Corydalis yanhusuo could accelerate the in vivo distribution of alkaloid components in the formula, elevate the plasma concentration, and prolong the in vivo retention time of coumarin components. The synergistic effects of the two types of active ingredients endow the vinegar-processed Yuanhu Zhitong Formula with significantly superior antigastric ulcer activity compared with the raw formula. Moreover, network pharmacology results revealed that this formula exerts therapeutic effects against gastric ulcers mainly by regulating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This study clarified the optimal processing technology and the pharmacodynamic material basis of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula against gastric ulcers, confirmed the efficacy-enhancing effect of processing, and provided data support for the formulation of its processing production standards and clinical medication.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is a common vaginal infection in women of reproductive age and is often linked to a vaginal microbiota imbalance. Conventional antibiotics such as metronidazole are effective but are associated with side effects and recurrence, prompting interest in herbal alternatives.

Objectives

To compare the clinical efficacy of medicinal plants versus metronidazole in the treatment of bacterial vaginosis using evidence from randomized clinical trials.

Methods

This narrative review examined randomized clinical trials evaluating herbal interventions for bacterial vaginosis. Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect were searched for studies published up to March 2026. The included studies assessed herbal interventions administered orally or vaginally, alone or with conventional metronidazole therapy. Information on plant species, study design, participants, diagnostic criteria, interventions, results, and conclusions was extracted and synthesized narratively.

Results

Twenty-four published articles were included, covering a range of medicinal plants, including Allium sativum, Myrtus communis, Quercus species, Berberis vulgaris, Zataria multiflora, Calendula officinalis, Cymbopogon olivieri, and others. Herbal therapies showed efficacy comparable to or superior to metronidazole, with fewer side effects and lower recurrence rates. Their effects are attributed to bioactive compounds, including allicin, curcumin, berberine, tannins, flavonoids, and essential oils, which exhibit antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties.

Conclusions

Medicinal plants appear to be safe and effective alternatives or adjuncts for bacterial vaginosis; however, the heterogeneity in study designs and short follow-up periods limits definitive conclusions. Further well-designed, multicenter randomized trials with standardized protocols and long-term follow-up, along with studies exploring individual plants and their mechanisms of action, are needed to confirm efficacy, safety, and reproducibility and to support evidence-based use.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Caffeine is consumed for its presumed cognitive benefits, yet controlled studies have repeatedly failed to find effects on inhibitory control. Cross-sectional work suggests that people with elevated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms may benefit from chronic, moderate caffeine consumption, but whether acute intake improves cognition in proportion to symptom severity has not been tested experimentally.

Aims

We tested whether 250 mg of caffeine improves active inhibition (withholding a prepared response) and reactive inhibition (resolving response conflict), and whether ADHD symptom severity moderates these effects.

Methods

In a preregistered, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, a nonclinical sample of 36 young adults received 250 mg of caffeine or placebo in counterbalanced order, with testing 45 min after ingestion. Active inhibition was assessed with a Go/No-Go task (204 trials), reactive inhibition with an arrow flanker task (200 trials) and symptoms with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale. Mixed-effects models included treatment, symptom severity, their interaction and ten covariates; Bayes factors quantified evidence for the null.

Results

Both tasks produced their benchmark effects (dz = 1.24 and 1.09) and all indices were reliable (split-half r = 0.73-0.98). Caffeine affected neither commission errors (BF01 = 4.98), response criterion (5.14), Go reaction time (2.83), reaction time variability (4.35), flanker reaction time (5.49) nor flanker accuracy (5.09). ADHD symptoms moderated no effect (15 preregistered tests; smallest p = 0.514), yet predicted performance itself (flanker accuracy r = -0.42), indicating that the null is not due to an insensitive measure.

Conclusions

Caffeine produced no acute benefit for either form of inhibition, and ADHD symptoms did not moderate its effects. Bayes factors supported the absence rather than the nondetection of these effects, arguing against an acute improvement of inhibitory control that scales with ADHD symptom severity in nonclinical young adults. Whether this also holds for chronic consumption or for adults with diagnosed ADHD remains to be tested.

Objective

Caffeine could improve cognitive functions, but study protocols usually prohibit drinking coffee before cognitive testing. However, regular coffee consumers may experience withdrawal effects when they cannot drink their habitual coffee, which may impair cognitive performance. Therefore, we tested the effects of overnight coffee abstinence in regular coffee consumers: once allowing to drink their coffee and once not drinking coffee. The cognitive performance was compared with non-regular coffee consumers.

Methods

Thirty regular coffee consumers (RCCs) and 25 non-regular consumers (N-RCCs) took part in this study. RCCs were tested after their habitual morning coffee (c-RCC) and after overnight abstinence (a-RCC); N-RCCs were tested once. A cognitive battery assessed reaction time (RT), processing speed (digit symbol substitution test), working memory, verbal learning/memory and executive function (Stroop). Sleep quality was included as a covariate.

Results

Fifty-nine male athletes were stratified into power (n = 30) and endurance (n = 29) groups, then randomly assigned to a whey protein group (WG) or a placebo control group (CG). Biomarkers assessed pre- and post-intervention included alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), C-reactive protein (CRP), and creatine kinase (CK). Significant reductions in ALT, AST, and CK were observed in both endurance- and power-trained athletes after supplementation (p = 0.001, p = 0.015, p = 0.001, and p = 0.003 respectively), indicating attenuated hepatic and muscular stress. Among the four biomarkers, only ALT displayed a statistically significant three-way interaction (Time × Supplementation × Training modality; p = 0.003), identifying it as the sole marker showing a genuine modality-specific differential response to supplementation. A significant within-group reduction in CRP was additionally observed in the supplemented power-trained athletes (p = 0.039), whereas endurance athletes showed only minor, non-significant changes; because the omnibus three-way interaction for CRP was not significant, this finding is reported as a within-group trend rather than evidence of a differential effect between modalities. Placebo groups demonstrated stable or increased enzyme and CRP values, particularly in endurance athletes. These findings suggest that whey protein may attenuate exercise-induced hepatic and muscular stress across training modalities, with a modality-specific effect on hepatic stress markers (ALT) observed in power-trained athletes. The results highlight whey protein's potential as a nutritional aid to promote recovery and physiological adaptation, possibly mediated by antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Purpose

Insomnia is a prevalent neurological disorder often caused by stress, anxiety, and imbalances in the GABAergic system. Although benzodiazepines like diazepam (DZP) are commonly prescribed, their long-term use is associated with adverse effects, including dependence and impaired coordination. Therefore, there is growing interest in natural alternatives with safer pharmacological profiles.

Method

This study aimed to investigate the sedative-like potential of L (+)-tartaric acid (LTA), a naturally occurring organic acid, through both in vivo and in silico approaches targeting the γ-aminobutyric acid A (GABAA) receptor. Sedative-like activity was evaluated in Swiss albino mice using thiopental sodium-induced sleeping time, open-field, and rotarod tests.

Findings

LTA significantly reduced sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration in a dose-dependent manner, with the higher dose (240 mg/kg) producing a more pronounced effect. Co-administration of LTA with DZP further enhanced thiopental-induced hypnosis. In the open-field test, LTA reduced locomotor and exploratory activities, as evidenced by decreases in square crossings, rearing, and grooming behaviors. Rotarod assessment demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction in motor coordination and neuromuscular performance, although the impairment remained less pronounced than that produced by DZP at the lower tested dose. Molecular docking revealed lower binding affinity than DZP but demonstrated multiple hydrogen-bond (HB) interactions with key amino acid (AA) residues of the GABAA receptor, suggesting a potentially stable receptor interaction.

Conclusion

Collectively, the behavioral and computational findings indicate that LTA possesses sedative-like properties and may modulate GABAergic neurotransmission. Further mechanistic, pharmacokinetic, and electrophysiological studies are required to clarify its precise mode of action and therapeutic potential.

raw.abstractText: The collagen triple helix is the most abundant protein structural motif in animals. It tolerates any amino acid in its Xaa and Yaa positions but demands glycine (Gly) at every third position, where the residue packs into the sterically forbidding core of the triple helix and donates the recurring interstrand N-H⋯OC hydrogen bond that stitches the three strands together. (2S)-Proline (Pro) and (2S,4R)-4-hydroxyproline (Hyp) are enriched far above their proteome-wide abundance because they preorganize individual strands into the polyproline II conformation, lowering the entropic cost of folding. We asked whether the triple helix is intrinsically stable enough to form from strands that carry no such preorganization, that is, from polyglycine. To offset the conformational entropy of a Gly-rich tract, we embedded Gly<sub>6</sub> within flanking triple-helical (Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>n</sub> clamps in Ac-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>6</sub>-Gly<sub>6</sub>-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>5</sub>-Pro-Hyp-NH<sub>2</sub> and compared it with an otherwise identical peptide in which Gly<sub>6</sub> was replaced by two [2-(2-aminoethoxy)ethoxy]acetic acid units, a flexible, length-matched spacer that lacks most of the regularly spaced backbone amides of Gly<sub>6</sub>. Circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the diagnostic positive band at 225 nm. The molar ellipticity of the spacer-containing control was 86% of that of the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, matching the 35/41 = 85% ratio of residues capable of triple-helix formation and consistent with the Gly<sub>6</sub> segment contributing to the triple-helical signal. Thermal denaturation yielded a T<sub>m</sub> of 46.8°C for the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, 6.3°C higher than that of the matched spacer control. This added stability indicates that the polyglycine tract is not merely accommodated within the helix but contributes stabilizing interstrand hydrogen bonds. Together, these data indicate that three polyglycine strands can form a collagen triple helix when flanked by triple-helical clamps. This result is consistent with the idea that the triple-helical architecture predates the recruitment of Pro and Hyp, informs the evolutionary origin of collagen, and offers a blunt-ended, symmetric scaffold for designing peptidic triple helices.

Background

Prolonged exposure to hepatotoxic antiretroviral therapy (ART) could lead to chronic liver injury, which might increase risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We used causal inference methods to evaluate if cumulative exposure to ART with known mechanisms of chronic liver injury is associated with HCC among people with HIV (PWH), by chronic liver disease (CLD) status.

Methods

We conducted a cohort study of antiretroviral-naive PWH with and without diagnosed CLD who initiated ART in the Veterans Affairs between 1999 and 2023. Exposure to ART with known mechanism of chronic liver injury (mitochondrial toxicity or accumulation of toxic intermediates) was determined monthly through prescription fills. Incident HCC was identified by Veterans Affairs National Cancer Registry and/or recorded diagnoses. Marginal structural models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of HCC associated with cumulative exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART compared with ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms, by CLD status.

Results

Among 11,854 PWH without CLD and 6771 PWH with CLD, we observed 112 and 378 HCC events, respectively. Among PWH without CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was associated with HCC when compared with ≥4 years of use of ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms (OR = 4.02 [95% CI: 1.00-16.24]). Among PWH with CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was not associated with HCC (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.68-2.72).

Conclusion

Four or more years of ART with a chronic liver injury mechanism was associated with HCC among PWH without CLD, but not those with CLD.

Purpose

To investigate the microbial species latent in corneas of healthy individuals and determine whether small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) serves as a risk factor for pathogen reactivation.

Setting

Ophthalmology Department of Peking University Third Hospital, Beijing, China.

Design

Prospective cohort study.

Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was used to analyze the microbial composition of corneal lenticules from SMILE. Based on the results, patients were categorized into viral group (VG) and nonviral pathogen group (NVPG). 2 Matched groups (MG1 and MG2) were established by selecting pathogen-negative individuals at a 1:4 ratio relative to 2 positive groups. raw.abstractText: Melatonin (MEL) is an endogenous hormone that regulates circadian rhythm, immune function and oxidative stress responses. Norepinephrine (NE), an endogenous catecholamine, increases blood pressure through the sympathetic nervous system and is commonly administered intraoperatively or in the clinically ill patient for hemodynamic support. A secondary analysis was conducted using data from a prospective, single-centre, cross-over study involving volunteers who received stepwise NE infusions while awake and under total intravenous general anaesthesia. Arterial blood samples were collected to determine plasma MEL and NE concentrations. Linear mixed-effects modelling was used to assess the relationship between NE and MEL concentrations. A total of 36 healthy volunteers were enroled, yielding 417 MEL-NE samples. Intravenous NE administration was significantly associated with higher plasma MEL concentration, corresponding to an estimated 26% increase in MEL per 1 standard-deviation increase in NE concentration (Estimate = 0.230, p < 0.001). MEL concentrations were approximately 43% higher in the awake phase compared to GA (Estimate = 0.356, p < 0.001). GA did not significantly modify the NE-MEL association (Estimate = -0.02877, p = 0.528). Substantial positive correlation was observed between baseline MEL concentrations and the magnitude of the response to NE administration (r = 0.74). In conclusion, intravenous NE increases plasma MEL concentrations in both awake and anaesthetised individuals. Substantial interindividual variation in MEL response suggests underlying physiological differences. Future studies should explore the long-term effects of NE administration on MEL concentrations. Background

Sleep deprivation and poor sleep quality are critical problems among intensive care unit (ICU) patients, with significant implications for recovery, delirium onset and clinical outcomes. Despite growing scientific interest, no bibliometric study has systematically mapped the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this field.

Aim

To analyse the bibliometric characteristics and thematic structure of publications on sleep deprivation, sleep promotion and sleep quality in ICU patients indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database between 1983 and 2026.

Study design

A descriptive and evaluative bibliometric analysis was conducted. Data were retrieved on April 26, 2026, from the WoS Core Collection using a comprehensive search strategy. Publications were filtered by document type, WoS categories (nursing, critical care medicine, anaesthesiology) and index (SCI-EXPANDED, SSCI, ESCI). Data were analysed using R software with the Biblioshiny interface, and annual publication trends were evaluated using Microsoft Excel.

Results

Of 11 418 publications retrieved, 379 met the inclusion criteria, spanning 37 years (1983-2026). Linear regression revealed a statistically significant positive trend in publication output (β = 0.643, R2 = 0.704, r = 0.839, p < 0.001), with mean annual publications of 10.24 ± 8.83 and notable acceleration from the 2000s onwards. Thematic mapping identified 'sleep', 'sleep deprivation' and 'delirium' as motor themes both highly central and well developed. Emerging concepts included circadian rhythm, actigraphy, fatigue, pain and anxiety.

Conclusions

ICU sleep research has grown substantially over four decades, with sleep deprivation and delirium emerging as co-dominant research priorities. Thematic gaps and emerging clusters identified in this analysis highlight important directions for future nursing research and evidence-based practice development in critical care.

Relevance to clinical practice

This bibliometric analysis identified sleep deprivation and delirium as the co-dominant motor themes of ICU sleep research, and intervention-related concepts such as earplugs, eye masks and melatonin as emerging clusters. These evidence-based trends can guide ICU nurses in prioritizing targeted sleep promotion protocols and support policymakers in directing resources toward the most scientifically mature intervention areas in critical care.

raw.abstractText: Preterm white matter injury (PWMI) is a serious neurologic condition that threatens neonatal survival and severely impairs the cognitive and motor development of affected children. Melatonin (Mel), a neuroendocrine hormone with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, has shown neuroprotective potential in neonatal brain injury, although the mechanisms underlying its effects in PWMI remain incompletely understood. Collectively, these findings suggest that Mel facilitates oligodendrogenesis and white matter repair after PWMI, at least in part through modulation of the AKT/GSK-3β/β-catenin pathway. Multimodal MRI can provide a useful noninvasive approach for monitoring treatment-related changes in white matter injury and development, supporting further investigation of Mel as a potential therapeutic strategy for PWMI.

raw.abstractText: TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK, the TAM receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), play roles in phagocytosis and negative regulation of immune responses, contributing to homeostasis in many adult tissues. Aberrant TAM signaling leads to diseases including autoimmune disorders, viral infection, inflammation, and cancer. Development of successful drugs targeting TAM receptors is hindered by incomplete knowledge of the receptor activation mechanism. Receptor dimerization is assumed to play a role, as seen for most RTKs. However, full biological responses require the TAM ligands to engage phosphatidylserine in an opposing cell or virus membrane, suggesting a more complex mechanism, possibly involving higher-order receptor oligomerization or clustering. Here, we present an X-ray crystal structure of the ectodomain of MERTK, which adopts a highly curved conformation with key interdomain boundaries stabilized by N-linked glycan moieties. We show that this MERTK extracellular region (ECR) forms a similar conformation in solution using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), which also suggests a flexible ECR. We compare these crystallographic and solution data for MERTK with SAXS and AlphaFold structural predictions for the other two TAM receptors. SAXS data confirm that each TAM ECR has a distinct curvature, with TYRO3 the most bent and AXL relatively straight. This leads us to speculate that these different ectodomain conformations guide receptor-specific functions. The MERTK X-ray crystal structure also suggests a head-to-tail intermolecular interaction between the Ig2 domain of one MERTK and the FNIIIb domain of a second that has intriguing parallels with interactions that have been proposed to regulate Eph receptor clustering.

raw.abstractText: Activity-guided separation of medicinal plants requires linking activity signals and chromatographic resolution in complex matrices. In this study, based on a previously established HPLC-DPPH platform, medium-pressure prefractionation and preparative chromatographic purification were applied for the targeted isolation of free radical scavengers from Saxifraga tangutica (S. tangutica). Medium-pressure prefractionation reduced sample complexity and enriched active fractions, while Click XION chromatography concentrated the target fraction. Subsequent purification on the ReproSil-Pur C18 AQ column resolved this fraction into two baseline-separated active peaks, affording compounds with purities greater than 95%. The isolated compounds were identified as quercetin-3-O-β-D-glucoside-7-O-β-D-glucoside and quercetin-3-O-β-D-galactoside-7-O-β-D-glucoside, a pair of C-4″-epimeric quercetin 3,7-di-O-glycosides. Both compounds exhibited DPPH radical-scavenging activity, with IC<sub>50</sub> values of 68.94 ± 2.77 and 75.59 ± 2.14 μM, respectively. DFT calculations, molecular docking, and ADMET prediction further supported the comparative interpretation of their electronic features, antioxidant-related interaction potential, and predicted pharmacokinetic profiles. Overall, this study achieved the activity guided isolation and activity evaluation of a pair of high-purity C-4″-epimeric flavonol diglycosides from S. tangutica, providing a practical chromatographic strategy for the targeted characterization of structurally similar bioactive constituents from medicinal plants.

raw.abstractText: Breast cancer (BC) has become the most prevalent cancer worldwide, and BC patients have the highest rate of depression of all cancer patients. However, previous studies, especially studies based on clinical sample data, have failed to reveal exactly how depression affects BC. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) was used to determine the causal relationship between depression and BC. Transcriptomics and metabolomics were used to analyze BC samples from nondepressed and depressed patients and to validate differentially expressed genes and key metabolites in vitro. Molecular docking techniques were used to identify compounds that regulate key targets and validate the functions of the compounds in in vitro and in vivo animal models. Depression was identified as a risk factor for BC by the TSMR analysis. On the basis of clinical samples, for the first time, we identified PPARγ and norepinephrine (NE) as key genes and metabolites that mediate the pro-BC effects of depression. In addition, we demonstrated that quercetin can target PPARγ and reverse the procancer effects of PPARγ inhibition mediated by chronic stress in BC cells. Moreover, we found that PPARγ may be associated with the inhibition of CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment. In conclusion, depression can increase the infiltration level of NE in tumors and inhibit the expression of PPARγ in tumor cells, thus promoting the proliferation of BC cells and inhibiting the infiltration of CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells in the immune microenvironment, ultimately leading to accelerated tumor growth. Quercetin can target PPARγ and reverse this cancer-promoting process.

raw.abstractText: Vitamin D is a nutrient and prohormone obtained from diet and supplements and synthesized in the skin. It is essential for calcium and phosphate homeostasis and skeletal health and influences multiple extra-skeletal processes, yet deficiency remains common worldwide. This narrative review summarizes vitamin D sources, physiology, metabolism, pharmacokinetics, clinical relevance and safety and outlines the distinct pharmacokinetic profiles and clinical roles of vitamin D, calcidiol and calcitriol and its analogues. Evidence consistently supports vitamin D, combined with calcium, for preventing and treating deficiency-related skeletal disorders in high-risk populations, and in specific conditions such as malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism and frailty. In vitamin D-replete populations, large trials show limited extra-skeletal benefits, apart from modest effects on cancer mortality and progression from prediabetes to Type 2 diabetes. Untargeted screening is not recommended. Future research should prioritize targeted supplementation, standardized assays and identification of populations most likely to benefit from supplementation.

raw.abstractText:
Background

The results of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) regarding the effect of vitamin D supplementation on mortality reduction are conflicting.

Objective

The aim of this study was to assess the level of evidence through a sensitivity analysis of the meta-analysis by Shah et al. (2024) using the Rebuilt the Evidence Base (REB) method.

Methods

The main inclusion criterion was a double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT design. The exclusion criteria were trials combining vitamin D with other nutrients and unpublished RCTs. The main outcome was all-cause mortality. A bias analysis was performed, followed by a hypothetico-deductive analysis to determine the confirmatory or exploratory nature of each RCT. The REB method was used to interpret the results and assess the level of evidence.

Results

Among the 25 RCTs included in the meta-analysis by Shah et al., the analysis was performed on 8 RCTs at low risk of bias including 30 320 participants. Seven RCTs raised some concerns, and two RCTs were at high risk of bias according to ROB2. Bias arose from the randomization process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, and selection of the reported results. The results were statistically significant, in favor of vitamin D supplementation: RR = 0.96 (95% CI [0.92, 1.00]), p = 0.04. No RCT was conclusive.

Conclusion

According to the REB method, there is an evidence signal regarding the benefit of vitamin D supplementation in the population aged 75 and older, which remains to be confirmed.

raw.title: An ROS-responsive photosynthetic biosystem disrupts the infectious-inflammatory-hypoxic cycle in pneumonia
raw.authorString: Huang L, Yan Z, Li K, Xu W, Ming R, Wang Z, Li C, Chen H, Liu S, Jing Y, Zhang R, Shi Y, Pan Y, Tian J, Jin P, Li J.
raw.abstractText: Acute lung injury (ALI) is sustained by a self-reinforcing cycle of inflammation, oxidative stress and hypoxia that current therapies cannot fully disrupt. To break this cycle, we engineered Haematococcus pluvialis (Hae) with chemiluminescent peroxyoxalate (CPPO) and fluorophore (Cy5) to construct a ROS-responsive photosynthetic biosystem (Hae@CC) for ALI therapy. Upon nebulization, excess H2O2 at the lesion triggers chemiluminescence (CL), which activates Cy5 through resonance energy transfer and drives endogenous Hae photosynthesis to produce oxygen (O₂) and the antioxidant astaxanthin (AST). In both lipopolysaccharide (LPS)- and bacteria-induced murine ALI models, aerosolized Hae@CC reduces bacterial load, alleviates pulmonary oedema and inflammation, promotes M2-biased macrophage polarization, enhances angiogenesis and improves pulmonary function, outperforming dexamethasone across multiple endpoints, with no appreciable toxicity in vivo. By correcting local hypoxia and redox imbalance, this biosystem resets the alveolar microenvironment, establishing that restoring homeostatic control, rather than blocking individual mediators, resolves inflammatory tissue injury.

raw.abstractText: Gymnema sylvestre R.Br. and Berberis aristata DC. are two widely used Ayurvedic antihyperglycemic herbs that are frequently co-formulated in polyherbal preparations, yet reference HPTLC identity data for their hydroalcoholic extracts remain limited. This study reports a preliminary qualitative HPTLC fingerprinting investigation of the hydroalcoholic extract of Gymnema sylvestre and the hydroalcoholic and aqueous extracts of Berberis aristata . For Gymnema sylvestre extract (leaf, 14% w/w hydroalcoholic yield), chromatography on silica gel 60 F₂₅₄ with toluene: ethyl acetate: formic acid: methanol (3:5:0.5:2) and post-derivatization visualization (10% sulphuric acid in methanol) resolved three bands at Rf 0.52, 0.33 and 0.19, developing light blue, dark blue and light blue colouration respectively, consistent with an oleanane-type triterpenoid saponin class and tentatively corresponding by co-chromatography to gymnemagenin, gymnemic acid IV and deacyl gymnemic acid. For Berberis aristata extracts (root; hydroalcoholic yield 8% w/w, aqueous yield 6% w/w), the mobile phase butanol: ethyl acetate: formic acid: water (3:5:0.5:1) resolved two bands at Rf 0.58 and 0.47 in both extracts, showing yellowish-green fluorescence under UV light (254/366 nm) without derivatization, consistent with the protoberberine alkaloid chromophore and tentatively corresponding to berberine and palmatine; the jatrorrhizine standard resolved at a distinct Rf of 0.52 but was not detected in either extract. These preliminary, tentative fingerprints are reported as a qualitative reference profile only; quantitative estimation, inter-batch replication, and formal validation remain necessary before these methods can be regarded as standardization tools.

raw.abstractText: Gαo is the most prevalent G protein α subunit in the brain and is critical for signal transduction through G protein-coupled receptors. Mutations in the gene encoding Gαo (  GNAO1 ) cause a rare neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements (NEDIM) and, in some patients, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). Here, we integrate human genetic analysis with cellular assays to define mechanistic classes of  GNAO1 mutations and in vivo approaches to evaluate therapeutic strategies. We grouped variants into two functional categories: those predicted to sequester Gβγ and those with reduced Gαo expression and therefore increased Gβγ signaling. Analysis of patient data revealed that mutations predicted to impair Gβγ release are significantly associated with NEDIM. Using the  GNAO1 R209H/+ mouse as a model of NEDIM, we evaluated two small molecules: caffeine, a nonselective adenosine receptor antagonist, and gallein, a selective modulator of Gβγ–effector interactions. Both compounds significantly reduced hyperlocomotion in the open field test. Whole–cell patch–clamp electrophysiology revealed sex- and cell type–specific hyperexcitability in spiny projection neurons within the dorsolateral striatum of  GNAO1 R209H/+ mice. Together, these findings implicate dysfunction of dorsolateral striatal pathways in GNAO1–related disorder and suggest that mechanistic understanding of disease variants can guide targeted therapeutic strategies.

raw.abstractText: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is a common clinical endocrine and metabolic disorder. Its clinical phenotype spectrum is undergoing a profound shift, evolving from the classic, severe presentations characterized by bone and kidney involvement towards more occult and subclinical forms. With the increasing adoption of routine biochemical screening and advancements in diagnostic technologies, there has been a notable rise in subclinical phenotypes of PHPT in China, particularly asymptomatic PHPT and normocalcemic PHPT. This trend not only reflects the progress of Chinese public health system but also imposes higher demands for precision in clinical diagnosis and treatment. Meanwhile, preoperative localization techniques have evolved from traditional ultrasound and radionuclide scanning to the era of four-dimensional CT and choline positron emission tomography, laying a solid foundation for the widespread adoption of minimally invasive parathyroidectomy. However, the clinical management of PHPT in China still faces significant challenges, including insufficient awareness among primary care physicians, imbalanced accessibility to advanced imaging equipment, and the complexity of managing multi-gland disease. This review systematically examines relevant literature published both domestically and internationally in recent years. It aims to outline the theoretical evolution, technological advancements, and disease characteristics specific to the Chinese population, with the goal of providing a reference for the standardized diagnosis and treatment of PHPT in China.

raw.abstractText:
Background

In the United States, sexual and gender minority people (SGMP), including lesbian-, gay-, bisexual-, and transgender-identifying individuals, report disproportionately higher rates of illicit single substance use and polysubstance use compared to their heterosexual and cisgender counterparts. We conducted a qualitative analysis to better understand the disparate polysubstance use-related outcomes among SGMP reported in the extant literature. Our research question was: How and why do SGM people who inject drugs engage in polysubstance use?

Methods

We conducted semi-structured interviews with SGMP assigned male at birth (n = 15). Eligibility criteria included sex with men and injection drug use and/or opioid use in the last two years. Data were collected at a community site associated with a syringe services program in Los Angeles, CA between May 2022 and November 2022.

Results

All participants reported lifetime polysubstance use and discussed use of: (1) methamphetamines to meet increased energy demands of living in materially insecure risk environments followed by opioids for energy management and to prevent "overamping;" (2) methamphetamine to enhance sexual drive and experiences followed by opioids, cannabis, or gamma-hydroxybutyrate use to balance stimulant effects; and (3) multiple substances (such as opioids, methamphetamine, cocaine, alcohol) for mood management, emotional regulation, and managing past traumatic experiences.

Conclusions

Our findings describe and contextualize drivers of polysubstance use patterns among SGMP experiencing significant intersectional stressors exacerbated by material needs insecurity. Interventions must comprehensively integrate basic needs, mental health, substance use, and sexual health services to address inequitable polysubstance use-related health outcomes among SGMP.

raw.title: Resource availability reshapes clonal recovery and trait coordination across fragment configurations of Salvinia natans
raw.authorString: Su H, Bai Y, Zheng W, Liu X, Li P, Zhang M.
raw.abstractText: Background Clonal aquatic plants can regenerate from fragments, but how light and nutrient availability influence recovery across fragment configurations remains poorly understood. We conducted a four-week factorial experiment with the floating fern Salvinia natans , combining two light levels, two nutrient levels and three configurations: light fragmentation (LF; two three-node fragments), moderate fragmentation (MF; three two-node fragments) and severe fragmentation (SF; six single-node fragments). Initial total node number was standardized across configurations, with five replicate pots per treatment combination. We measured growth, biomass allocation and frond-specific metabolism, and examined trait coordination using plant trait multilayer networks (PTMNs). Results Under high-light, nutrient-rich conditions, MF produced more frond pairs and ramets and accumulated more dry weight than LF or SF. Under low light, dry-weight accumulation remained low and differences among configurations narrowed. High light combined with low nutrients was associated with higher carbohydrate concentrations and a greater submerged-frond to floating-frond dry-weight ratio. PTMNs showed contrasting patterns of trait coordination: LF had the greatest cross-layer connectivity, MF the strongest local clustering, and SF the highest module interlayer association. Carbohydrate traits and biomass allocation occupied central network positions, with the leading hubs differing among configurations. Conclusions The growth advantage of MF depended on resource availability. Fragment configurations were also associated with distinct relationships among carbohydrate status, tissue allocation and clonal growth. These findings show that recovery responses differed in both growth performance and the coordination of traits across functional layers.

raw.abstractText: Calcium (Ca²⁺) signaling is essential for neurotransmitter release, synaptic plasticity, gene expression, and neuronal excitability. Nicotine, the addictive component of tobacco, activates nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs), including alpha4ß2- and a7-containing receptor subtypes, thereby altering neuronal Ca²⁺ entry. ATP2B2 encodes plasma membrane calcium-transporting ATPase 2 (PMCA2), a neuronal high-affinity Ca²⁺ extrusion pump that helps shape local Ca²⁺ microdomains. Published work has shown that PMCA2 functionally associates with a7-nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (alpha7-nAChRs) through postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD-95) and can influence a7-nAChR surface expression. Genetic and transcriptomic studies have also linked ATP2B2-related pathways to substance use phenotypes, but there is no direct evidence that chronic nicotine alters PMCA2 expression. This narrative review distinguishes established findings from indirect evidence and untested predictions. We propose a mechanistic hypothesis in which chronic nicotine exposure may establish a new calcium-homeostatic equilibrium characterized by alpha7-nAChR downregulation and compensatory PMCA2 upregulation. We also hypothesize that, during early withdrawal, persistently elevated PMCA2 activity could contribute to excessive Ca²⁺ extrusion, reduced presynaptic glutamate release, cognitive impairment, and relapse vulnerability. These predicted effects require direct testing in nicotine exposure and withdrawal models. This review aims to examine the roles of calcium signaling and homeostasis in nicotine addiction, with particular emphasis on ATP2B2, which encodes the calcium ion pump PMCA2, and alpha7-nAChR.

raw.abstractText: Background. Change in cognitive control is a candidate transdiagnostic mechanism of psychedelic therapy. One account predicts that, once acute effects resolve, psilocybin shifts control toward flexibility while sparing inhibition and working memory. A motivational account (PRISM) predicts that psilocybin increases the willingness to exert control rather than the ability to do so. We tested both in patients with co-occurring alcohol use disorder (AUD) and major depression.  Methods. In this secondary analysis of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of psilocybin for AUD with comorbid major depressive disorder (MDD; ClinicalTrials.gov  NCT04620759 ), a subset of participants (placebo n=13, psilocybin n=12) completed five cognitive tasks before drug administration and again about one week after it (mean 6.7 days, SD 1.1). Outcome measures spanned the stability-flexibility continuum. Free choice between levels of cognitive demand indexed the participant's willingness to exert control. Effect sizes and Bayes factors were used to estimate drug effects and associations with change in drinking and depressive symptoms across 34 retest measures.  Results. Relative to placebo, psilocybin slowed responding in cued task switching (learning-phase RT d=1.01, BF10=7.7; switch trials d=1.12, BF10=17). Psilocybin effects on feedback-driven measures were inconsistent in direction (7 of 11 toward flexibility); the largest was on perseveration, which rose less with practice under psilocybin than under placebo (d=-0.79, BF10=1.1). Other drug effects on the 34 retest measures had inconclusive Bayes factors (BF10=0.40-2.4), and none survived false discovery rate correction. Demand avoidance, analyzed separately from the 34 measures, showed no detectable drug effect (BF01=2.0). Baseline demand avoidance showed no detectable relation to performance but tracked depressive symptoms (rho=.71, BF10=24). Drinking fell in both arms, and on 15 of 17 stability-flexibility measures change toward stability accompanied drinking reduction (stability composite rho=-.64, BF10=29; rho=-.43 when change was adjusted for baseline scores). Lower baseline working-memory span predicted larger drinking reductions (BF10=19-25). Depressive symptoms fell more after psilocybin than after placebo (PHQ-9, d=-0.88, BF10=2.7), but their change was not associated with cognitive change or predicted by working-memory span.  Conclusions. About one week after dosing, psilocybin slowed cued task switching but had no consistent effect on feedback-driven flexibility, and there was no evidence of an effect on the willingness to exert effort. Drinking reduction was associated with increased, not reduced, cognitive stability, whereas improvement in depressive symptoms was not associated with cognitive change. These pilot estimates can guide adequately powered trials.

raw.abstractText: Background/Objectives : Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a multisystem condition associated with oxidative stress. Flavonoids were studied individually, but not comprehensively in the CKM framework. This study aimed to explore associations between flavonoid intake and CKM risk and to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Methods : This study assessed the associations between dietary flavonoid intake and CKM risk using dose–response modeling based on National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) dietary data. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were employed to predict quercetin targets and validate binding affinity with the hub oxidative stress genes. Results : The advanced CKM group exhibited lower intakes of flavones, flavonols, kaempferol and quercetin compared to the nonadvanced group ( P  < 0.05). Higher total flavonoids, flavonols and quercetin intake was associated with lower odds of advanced CKM stage. Nonlinear associations were observed, with intake levels corresponding to the lowest observed risk estimated at 449 mg/d for total flavonoids, 31 mg/d for flavonols, and 19 mg/d for quercetin. Eleven quercetin targets were identified; MPO and NOX4 were identified as oxidative stress candidates. Docking predicted binding affinities of − 9.4 and − 8.4 kcal/mol. Conclusions : Dietary quercetin intake is nonlinearly associated with lower odds of advanced CKM stage. These findings may suggest a potential role of quercetin in oxidative stress pathways via MPO and NOX4.

raw.authorString: Abdalla s, Hussein s, Tarawneh N, Ababneh N, Awidi A.
raw.abstractText: Introduction with high mortality rate, cutaneous melanoma (CM) is considered the most dangerous form of skin cancer, with steadily increasing incidence worldwide. Hormone-related therapies, especially those involving estrogen (E2), have emerged as promising strategies for treating CM. The phytoestrogens quercetin and luteolin have gained attention due to their antitumor effects across various cancers, including melanoma. However, the precise mechanisms by which they exert their effects and their association with G-protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) signaling in melanoma remain unclear. Methods we investigated the inhibitory effects of quercetin and luteolin in the MeWo melanoma cell line and their modulation of GPER-associated signaling. The effects of the flavonoids on cell viability, apoptosis and cell cycle were examined by MTT assay and flow cytometry. Cell migration was evaluated by transwell assay. GPER expression was verified by immunofluorescence staining, and the impact of the flavonoids on key signaling proteins was confirmed by Western blot. Results we showed that quercetin and luteolin exerted anti-proliferative and anti-migratory effects in melanoma cells. The two flavonoids also induced apoptosis and arrested the cell cycle at S and G2/M phases. Immunofluorescence and immunoblotting confirmed the presence of GPER in this cell line, and treatment with quercetin and luteolin, particularly at 100 µM, upregulated its expression. Quercetin and luteolin, as well as the GPER agonist G-1, enhanced the expression of P-ERK and c-Myc but reduced the expression of P-Akt. These responses were attenuated or reversed by the specific GPER antagonist G15, supporting a potential association between these effects and GPER signaling. Conclusion quercetin and luteolin have antitumor effects on the MeWo melanoma cell line in association with GPER signaling, suggesting that GPER-associated pathways are associated with their anti-melanoma effects and warrant further investigation.

raw.abstractText: Objective: To observe the inhibition of resveratrol on coal dust-induced pulmonary fibrosis and explore the possible mechanism. Methods: A mouse model of pneumoconiosis was established by coal dust inhalation, and resveratrol was administered as treatment. Lung inflammation and fibrosis were observed using hematoxylin/eosin (HE) and Masson staining, and hydroxyproline content was measured by colorimetric assay. In vitro, lung epithelial cells were exposed with coal dust alone or in combination with resveratrol. Cell migration and invasion abilities were assessed using wound healing assay and Transwell assay. The key molecules of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) were detected by western blotting and ELISA. Additionally, the effects of resveratrol on proliferation and collagen production in TGF-β1-stimulated fibroblasts were examined using EDU, CCK-8, and western blotting. Results: The coal dust group showed marked inflammatory cell infiltration, collagen deposition, and elevated hydroxyproline levels in lung tissue, all of which were significantly improved in the resveratrol-treated group. In vitro, coal dust increased the migration rate, invasive ability, downregulated E-cadherin, and upregulated N-cadherin, vimentin, and Snail of lung epithelial cells, whereas these cellular changes were markedly attenuated in the resveratrol-treated group. Moreover, the levels of TGF-β1 and TNF-α were significantly lower in the resveratrol-treated group than in the coal dust group. In fibroblasts, the cell proliferation rate and collagen (COL-1, COL-3, α-SMA) were lower in the resveratrol-treated group than in the TGF-β1-stimulated group. Conclusion: Resveratrol inhibited EMT in lung epithelial cells, reduced TGF-β1 and TNF-α release, suppressed fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transformation (FMT), and alleviated coal dust-induced pulmonary fibrosis.

raw.abstractText: Infectious disease emergence in natural systems is driven by complex host-pathogen-environment interactions. Nutritional factors, particularly dietary antioxidants, can modulate physiological states by enhancing immune function and mitigating oxidative damage, but the underlying molecular mechanisms in wildlife remain poorly understood. To bridge this gap, we conducted a transcriptomic analysis of blood samples from both healthy and clinically affected magnificent frigatebirds Fregata magnificens chicks treated with either resveratrol (a plant-derived polyphenol with known antiviral and antioxidant properties) or a placebo. Resveratrol supplementation induced significant gene expression changes, particularly in diseased individuals, where we identified the upregulation of ten key genes in treated sick chicks, including the interferon-stimulated genes (IFI6, OASL2) and immune regulators (SOCS1, PLAC8); two additional transcripts were unannotated. Furthermore, resveratrol treatment was associated with increased expression of DDX60, a potent antiviral factor, and CYGB1, which supports cytoprotection. In contrast, healthy chicks showed fewer differentially expressed genes, primarily associated with metabolism and cellular organization. Collectively, our results reveal a transcriptional signature consistent with dietary antioxidants such as resveratrol acting as active molecular modulators of host defense, rather than simple passive antioxidants, although direct evidence of enhanced antiviral protection (e.g. reduced viral load) remains to be established. This study highlights the utility of transcriptomic approaches to link nutritional ecology with disease dynamics, offering a framework for understanding how dietary quality shapes host defense strategies and population resilience under increasing pathogen pressure.

raw.abstractText: Treatment with low-dose ketamine is neuroprotective in rodent models of acute damage, while high doses of ketamine can be neurotoxic. Our group has previously shown that sub-anesthetic ketamine treatment leads to long-term reduction of L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID) via brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-signaling in a rat 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) model of Parkinson's disease (PD). In this report, we investigated if sub-anesthetic ketamine is also neuroprotective in a progressive 6-OHDA model of PD via neurotrophic action through the tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) receptor. We demonstrated that ketamine-treatment (20 mg/kg, i.p.) prior to striatal administration of the neurotoxin 6-OHDA is neuroprotective, providing near complete protection against development of parkinsonian motor deficits. This robust behavioral efficacy occurred in the presence of only modest preservation of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) striatal levels (~50-60% loss). Interestingly, based on data from an additional cohort treated with ketamine and ANA-12 (TrkB antagonist) we found that the neuroprotective effects of ketamine are not mediated by TrkB receptors. Semi-quantitative western analysis showed that the relative tyrosine hydroxylase content in the striatum was not significantly increased in ketamine-treated rats compared to vehicle. Unbiased stereology of dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) revealed no significant differences between any of the groups. The role of BDNF was evaluated with in situ hybridization for RNA of BDNF and TrkB. While BDNF expression was not changed, co-administration of ketamine and ANA-12 led to a significant decrease in TrkB receptor expression compared to ketamine-only on the lesioned but not the intact hemisphere in the SNc. In conclusion, we show that ketamine at the low dose currently pursued for therapeutic benefit for LID led to robust behavioral motor improvement in this rodent PD degeneration model, yet these protective effects were not driven by neurotrophic BDNF-signaling, indicating complex mechanisms are underlying neuroprotective activities of low-dose ketamine.

raw.abstractText: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) approach employs chemical analysis of municipal wastewater and provides a valuable data source for monitoring community-level illicit drug consumption. This study aimed to determine illicit drug residues in wastewater samples collected in eight cities located in the Greater Poland Voivodship (western Poland) to track patterns of illicit drug use across this region. The research filled the gap in WBE studies, in which Eastern European countries have been very poorly represented. The obtained data were also compared with the results of a similar study conducted by our research team in the years 2012-2014. Determination of illicit drugs and their metabolites was performed using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry. The method was validated and covered nine analytes, including amphetamine-type stimulants, cocaine and cannabis metabolites, and new psychoactive substances. Among the substances investigated, amphetamine exhibited the highest mass loads across all sampling days and cities. The conducted research confirmed the presence of new psychoactive substances in many cities of western Poland. The inter-day profiles of illicit drug residues in wastewater revealed substance-specific and city-dependent temporal patterns, with stimulant drugs and a cocaine metabolite exhibiting suggestive indications of weekend-associated increases. Most cities demonstrated an increase in the levels of drug residues in wastewater compared to levels determined 10 years ago. The current study highlights the capability of WBE to capture spatial heterogeneity and short-term and long-term fluctuations in illicit drug consumption.

raw.abstractText: Clonal Hematopoiesis (CH) affects the aging population and is associated with increased risk of hematological malignancy, cardiovascular disease, and all-cause mortality. Therapeutic options for CH remain limited. Using hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) color barcoding and mosaic mutagenesis in zebrafish, we identified perturbed choline metabolism and increased phosphatidylcholine (PC) biosynthesis via choline kinase alpha (CHKA) in asxl1-mutant HSPCs. Suppressing CHKA-dependent choline flux reduced ASXL1-driven clonal expansion. This effect was conserved in a murine DNMT3A and human TET2 model. Mechanistically, CHKA- dependent choline flux controls phosphatidylcholine production that supports platelet activating factor (PAF) production. Exogenous PAF overcomes the suppressive effect of CHKA inhibition in ASXL1 and TET2 models. We isolated primary, human HSPCs from the peripheral blood of patients with endogenous ASXL1 mutations and demonstrated that perturbing PAF signaling reduces their competitive potential in an ex vivo clonal competition assay. This CHKA/PAF axis is conserved in TET2-mutant HSPCs. Together, these findings identify a mutation agnostic metabolic dependency across the three most common CH genotypes and demonstrate that targeting the CHKA-dependent choline flux suppresses clonal expansion.

raw.abstractText: Filamentous fungi generate chemical diversity through several evolutionary strategies, including the elaboration of conserved biosynthetic intermediates into structurally distinct secondary metabolites. Emodin and its corresponding anthrone are central intermediates in fungal aromatic polyketide metabolism, yet the enzymatic logic that remodels these precursors into more complex scaffolds remains incompletely understood. To investigate this process, we examined an infection-responsive non-reducing polyketide synthase biosynthetic gene cluster (barc) from the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae predicted to encode an emodin-derived aromatic polyketide pathway. Heterologous reconstruction of the barc cluster in Aspergillus nidulans led to the production of the previously reported diphenyl ether barceloneic acid A (1) and the xanthene barceloneic acid C2 (2), together with two new compounds derived from 2, barceloneic acids D and E (3 and 4). Compound 3 is a cyclopentanone adduct of the xanthene 2, whereas 4 is a polyketide-indole hybrid, highlighting the chemical reactivity of the xanthene 2 scaffold. Through combinatorial heterologous expression and feeding assays, we identified a predicted glucose-methanol-choline oxidoreductase (BarcL) as the enzyme responsible for converting diphenyl ether 1 to xanthene 2. This defines a previously uncharacterised oxidative scaffold-remodelling step in barceloneic acid biosynthesis, revealing how an emodin-derived pathway can access a xanthene scaffold. Deletion of the backbone gene barcB in M. anisopliae did not significantly alter virulence towards Tenebrio molitor (mealworm) under the conditions tested, suggesting that barceloneic acids are not essential for pathogenicity in this insect model.

raw.abstractText: Cannabis research is advancing rapidly, yet fundamental questions persist regarding the optimal design of human studies to empirically assess the potential harms and benefits of cannabis. There exist central methodological differences between studies that rely on controlled dose paradigms, ensuring internal validity, and those that utilize naturalistic, self-administration approaches which better reflect real-world use. Controlled paradigms offer precision and regulatory alignment but fail to capture the complexity of real-world cannabis consumption. Naturalistic designs enhance ecological validity but introduce variability and pose challenges for dosing, safety, and replicability. This perspective article presents two methods: one emphasizing the scientific rigor and utility of controlled dose paradigms for regulatory outcomes (e.g., FDA), and the other advocating for naturalistic models that prioritize real-world relevance of legal market cannabis consumption which can inform policy decisions (e.g., guidelines around high THC concentrate). However, rather than representing competing alternatives, controlled laboratory and naturalistic paradigms occupy distinct positions within the evidentiary framework of cannabinoid research, each addressing scientific questions that the other cannot. An integrated methods section proposes ways to incorporate the best features of both approaches to advance cannabinoid science study design.

raw.abstractText: Triple-negative breast cancers frequently upregulate the serine synthesis pathway, rendering them resistant to exogenous serine/glycine restriction. To identify vulnerabilities that emerge under serine/glycine limitation, we performed a metabolic CRISPR dropout screen in resistant TNBC cells and identified mitochondrial folate metabolism as a critical dependency. These findings identify SLC25A32 as a potential therapeutic target to improve responses to dietary serine/glycine restriction in TNBC.

raw.abstractText:
The toxicity of the amino acids glycine and L-serine at high concentrations in bacteria was discovered decades ago. In this work, we used transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-seq) experiments to determine the genes necessary to tolerate excess L-serine, diglycine, or glycine in the human pathogen Staphylococcus aureus. Our results indicate that intracellular accumulation of specific counterbalancing amino acids-such as alanine in the presence of excess glycine-is the primary mechanism of resistance to amino acid toxicity. Consistent with this model, specific amino acid and peptide uptake transporters were required for fitness in each treatment; the peptide transporter DtpT was crucial for fitness in excess L-serine or glycine, and the alanine transporter AapA was necessary for fitness in diglycine. Tn-seq results also identified the cystine/cysteine uptake transporter TcyABC as necessary in excess L-serine, suggesting that both peptide and cysteine uptake contribute to L-serine tolerance. In addition to uptake mechanisms, glycine and diglycine toxicity is neutralized by D-alanine aminotransferase (Dat), which is required for D-alanine synthesis. The requirement for Dat and DtpT function-but not AapA-in excess glycine is explained by excess glycine inhibiting alanine uptake. Building on this finding, we found that combined treatment with glycine and the alanine analog antibiotic D-cycloserine was strongly synergistic in inhibiting S. aureus growth. Overall, our findings identify targetable mechanisms underlying excess amino acid tolerance in S. aureus, with implications for developing novel combination treatments using the accessible and biocompatible amino acids glycine and L-serine.

Importance

Growing evidence supports the beneficial effects of glycine and L-serine supplementation in combating bacterial infections. Previous researchers have found that combining antibiotic treatment with high glycine concentrations has additive effects with many antibiotics, even reversing resistance to antibiotics in some bacteria. In vivo, activating glycine and L-serine metabolism heightens the sensitivity of bacterial pathogens to the host complement system, and studies of glycine or L-serine treatments show low toxicity and reduced inflammation in mouse and human subjects. This study reveals that glycine may be an effective antibiotic adjuvant with D-cycloserine, and treatment with glycine or L-serine could potentiate other drugs that target alanine or cysteine metabolism, respectively.

raw.abstractText: Glycine is widely used as an excipient in protein-based biopharmaceutical formulations, yet its functions are often described too broadly, particularly in terms of stabilization. This review critically examines the physicochemical basis and formulation behavior of glycine across liquid, frozen, and freeze-dried systems, with emphasis on how its effects are governed by formulation composition, physical state, and processing history. Available evidence shows that glycine can contribute to several formulation functions, but its performance is highly product- and condition-dependent. In particular, crystallization represents a central feature of glycine-containing systems because it can support physical robustness and process performance while also creating risks associated with phase separation and loss of local stabilization. This benefit-risk balance depends on the extent of crystallization, the composition of the residual amorphous phase, and the surrounding formulation environment. These outcomes are further modified by interactions with sugars, buffers, surfactants, salts, and other excipients. Evidence from marketed protein-based biopharmaceutical products is also considered to place these mechanistic observations in a practical context. The review also identifies important evidence gaps, particularly in high-concentration protein formulations and in understanding how glycine physical state interacts with other formulation components. Overall, glycine is a multifunctional, physical-state- and process-dependent excipient, and its use should be supported by direct characterization of physical state and product-specific stability.
